searchText: I don't think so, the deposit index is 17K and they all look in batches as far as I looked to cook that is not trivial, the mempool of vanilla clients would prevent it from the same address, so you'll need to push them from different addresses or prepare your own block to include those txs you think a restart is enough? trying it now For Nimbus? should be I didn't check if it marked anything as `INVALID` when it shouldn't have. that's the condition under which Nimbus needs a restart, but I didn't see evidence of that so far (to be fair I didn't look) a restart seems to have helped https://panda-uploads-production.devops-539.workers.dev/panda/uploads/a0e182/glamsterdam-devnet-8-nimbus-besu-2-root-cause-report.html ^ dumped all the files to reproduce it later I'm seeing some inconsitencies between clients in how t hey are handling the eth/72 announced byte length causing downscoring, esp between besu, nethermind and geth the spec does not really specify this properly from what I can see we might need to update the spec to make it more precise? > `txsizeₙ` refers to the length of the 'consensus encoding' of a typed transaction, i.e. > the byte size of `tx-type || tx-data` for typed transactions, and the size of the > RLP-encoded `legacy-tx` for non-typed legacy transactions. what is consensus encoding? <https://github.com/ethereum/devp2p/blob/2c19a28b25c29487773ad6b07243e290fa8d65ec/caps/eth.md?plain=1#L524-L526> cc <@194432762315407360> where does geth implement this?
